statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH (yellow). The Nasdaq-100 cash index trades 29,242.44, down 0.43%, after printing a new session high of 29,285.50 against a 28,867.67 low and then easing about 43 points off it. The recovery leg from the 1.63% gap-down open still extends, which holds Tail at 21, but the first meaningful give-back of that leg keeps it from rising. Cross-asset amplifiers continue to decay: VIX 16.72 near its 16.58 session low, the 10-year 4.955% after tagging 5.012%, WTI $101.53 and Brent $105.73 off peaks near $104.79 and $109.44. Stress eases to 71.
recommendation: Tail at 21 sits in the watch band, so the mapped state is WATCH for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. The danger window is unchanged at 19:00-20:00 UTC, covering the final cash hour, where conditional Tail peaks at 23, two points below the block mapping. The conditional path returns to the low band across the post-close, overnight and Asian sessions, re-enters the watch band from Tuesday's European cash open, and reaches 23 again for the 13:30 UTC cash open. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: NDX extends to a new session high at 29,285.50 then gives back 43 points, the first real pause in the gap-recovery leg; VIX, the 10-year and crude all hold off their extremes, Tail holds at 21 in the watch band with 19:00-20:00 UTC retained as the danger window
body:
The recovery leg has extended once more and has now taken its first real pause. As of the 18:25 UTC quote the Nasdaq-100 cash index is at 29,242.44, down 126.00 points or 0.43% against a 29,368.44 previous close, having opened at 28,890.93 on a 1.63% gap. The session range is 28,867.67 to 29,285.50. The high is new: an hour ago the session peak stood at 29,257.57, and an hour before that at 29,208.57. The index now trades about 43 points below that high, the first give-back of any size since the low was set within minutes of the cash open and left untouched for roughly four and a half hours since.

That combination is why this assessment holds rather than moves. Continued extension into new session highs is the one genuine one-way element in the tape and is the structure that denies a reverse or grid approach the mean reversion it depends on, so Tail stays at 21 and in the watch band. But the leg is decelerating, and it is now retracing: 28 points of new high this hour against 49 in the previous one, followed by a 43-point pullback. A directional move that slows and then gives part of itself back is materially less pathological than one that holds its extreme, and that is the reason Tail is not raised. It is also held well below the block mapping because this structure remains the only amplifier present and because the index is still 0.43% below its previous close, which leaves a natural supply reference immediately overhead.

Every other element of the cross-asset picture continues to stabilise. VIX is quoted at 16.72, still up 5.56% against a 15.84 close, but sitting near its 16.58 session low after reaching 18.17. The 10-year Treasury yield printed 5.012% earlier today, its first touch of 5% since 2023, and has since fallen to 4.955%, below its 4.975% previous close and near the low end of a 4.934% to 5.012% range; the Federal Reserve H.15 release puts the 2-year at 4.56% and the 10-year at 4.95% for 10 September, and the effective federal funds rate at 3.63%, so the curve move is contained rather than a broad repricing. Crude has done the same: Brent reached about $109.44 and WTI about $104.79 during the European afternoon and are now quoted at $105.73 and $101.53. An amplifier that fails to extend after making its high is not adding to the probability of a no-retracement path, and an index grinding higher while implied volatility sits at session lows is describing low-realised-volatility drift rather than a violent impulse.

One element of the backdrop is firmer than it was and belongs on the record. Reporting from NBC News, International Business Times and The Motley Fool puts CME FedWatch odds of a quarter-point Federal Reserve rate hike on Wednesday above 90%, which would be the first increase since 2023 and would move the target range from 3.50-3.75% to 3.75-4.00%. The driver is Friday's consumer inflation print at 3.4% for August together with the oil move. This is a scheduled event two days beyond the end of this forecast window, so consistent with the published risk definitions it raises Stress and disciplines Confidence rather than lifting Tail; it also reinforces the bond market as the dominant cross-asset channel into midweek.

The catalyst stack is otherwise unchanged and re-verified from current reporting. Reuters reports Wall Street dropping as AI-safety worries pummel chipmakers, with the PHLX semiconductor index down 5.4%, Nvidia off 2.6% and Broadcom, Micron and AMD each down about 4%, after the heads of Anthropic, OpenAI and xAI called for a slower pace of frontier model development. The same session has cybersecurity and software names bid. Euronews reports that Saudi Arabia shut its East-West pipeline after drone attacks, that a merchant vessel was struck in the Strait of Hormuz on Sunday, and that flows through the strait have fallen from about 20 million barrels a day before the war to roughly 7 million; NBC News adds that officials expect the pipeline to be out of service for weeks and that Iran-Gulf talks scheduled for Monday were postponed.

That dispersion is the single most important reason the index is not trending in the conventional sense, and it is why the dominant mode is published as mixed rather than as a directional label. A market in which one industry is down more than 5% while another is bid is distributing risk internally rather than compressing it into one direction, and the index-level advance is the arithmetic of that rotation rather than a broad bid. Consistent with the published risk definitions, that conflict raises Stress and disciplines Confidence rather than forcing Tail higher. The shared cross-asset context file was checked and found stale and partial: it was collected at 14:26 UTC, about four hours before this assessment and well beyond the 90-minute freshness limit set by the inherited contract, and its collection status was reported as partial. It was therefore not used as supporting evidence, and all price levels, catalysts and the seven-day event list were verified independently from primary and reputable current sources.

The remaining live risks are event risks rather than path risks. The pipeline outage is physical and unrepaired, so a fresh Gulf headline can reprice crude in any hour, including the thin overnight session. Within the next 24 hours the scheduled set is light: weekly ADP employment at 12:15 UTC and the NY Empire State Manufacturing Index at 12:30 UTC on Tuesday, then a 20-year Treasury bond auction at 17:00 UTC, which with the 10-year near 5% is the clearest route from the rates complex into index risk inside the window. US Retail Sales at 12:30 UTC and the FOMC decision at 18:00 UTC both fall on Wednesday, beyond this window. Stress eases one point to 71, still firmly in the high band, and Confidence holds at 89: price, volatility, rates, energy, catalyst and calendar evidence is current and verified.

The danger window stays at 19:00 to 20:00 UTC, the final cash hour, unchanged from the previous two assessments. It is the point at which a day that has more than recovered its gap either confirms into the settlement or hands the advance back, and the moment at which a late crude headline would meet the thinnest liquidity of the cash session. Conditional Tail peaks at 23 there, two points below the block mapping, reflecting a scheduled transition and the single live path amplifier rather than any observed closing structure. Beyond it the conditional path returns to the low band overnight, re-enters the watch band from Tuesday's European cash open, and reaches 23 again at the 13:30 UTC cash open.

lookbackSummary: Over the past 24 hours the Claude series ran through the low band during Sunday's US evening, entered the watch band from 21:00 UTC as the AI-slowdown and Middle East supply stories developed, and reached the elevated band at 09:00 and 10:00 UTC when NQ set a sequence of lower lows under a trend-down mode. It stepped back to the watch band at 11:00 and 12:00 UTC, returned to the elevated band at 13:00 UTC when the first bounce faded into the cash open, then eased through 14:00, 15:00 and 16:00 UTC as the gap was absorbed, reaching 18 and the low band at 16:00 UTC before returning to 21 at 17:00 UTC when the retracement extended into new session highs. Stress declined steadily from 79 at the morning peak to 72, holding the high band throughout, and Confidence improved from 73 to 89 as live price evidence became available. All 24 hourly slots are available from published Claude history.
outlookSummary: The 24-hour outlook is built on an opening gap that has been more than fully retraced, with the index printing a new session high at 29,285.50 and then giving back about 43 points while VIX, the 10-year and crude all hold back from their session extremes. Conditional Tail holds at 21 through the remaining cash afternoon and peaks at 23 in the 19:00 UTC power hour that forms the published danger window. It then settles between 17 and 20 across the post-close, overnight and Asian sessions, with small uplifts where crude has typically repriced first on Middle East developments. The path re-enters the watch band at Tuesday's 07:00 UTC European cash open, dips into the midday lull, and peaks at 23 again for the 13:30 UTC cash open, two points below the block mapping. It eases into the FOMC-eve compression of the US afternoon and lifts to 21 for the 17:00 UTC 20-year bond auction. Confidence declines steadily with distance from the last verified price observation. Every hour beyond the current one is conditional risk, not observed structure.
